title_en: Regulations on Energy Conservation in Civil Buildings

articles.content_en: Article 1 These Regulations are formulated to strengthen the administration of energy conservation in civil buildings, reduce energy consumption during the use of civil buildings, and increase energy efficiency.

Article 2 For the purpose of these Regulations, "energy conservation in civil buildings" means activities to reduce energy consumption during the use of civil buildings while ensuring the service functions and indoor thermal environment quality of such buildings.
For the purpose of these Regulations, "civil buildings" means residential buildings, office buildings of state organs, and other public buildings used for commerce, services, education, health, etc.

Article 3 People's governments at all levels shall strengthen the leadership over the work of energy conservation in civil buildings, actively cultivate the service market for energy conservation in civil buildings, improve the service system for energy conservation in civil buildings, promote the development and application of technologies for energy conservation in civil buildings, and conduct publicity and education on knowledge of energy conservation in civil buildings.

Article 4 The State encourages and supports the use of renewable energy sources such as solar energy and geothermal energy in the construction of new buildings and the energy-saving renovation of existing buildings.
In areas with solar energy utilization conditions, relevant local people's governments and their departments shall take effective measures to encourage and support entities and individuals to install and use solar energy utilization systems such as solar water heating systems, lighting systems, heating systems, and air conditioning systems.

Article 5 The competent department of construction under the State Council shall be responsible for the supervision and administration of energy conservation in civil buildings nationwide. The competent departments of construction under local people's governments at or above the county level shall be responsible for the supervision and administration of energy conservation in civil buildings within their respective administrative regions.
The relevant departments of the people's governments at or above the county level shall be responsible for relevant work on energy conservation in civil buildings in accordance with the provisions of these Regulations and the division of duties prescribed by the people's government at the corresponding level.

Article 6 The competent department of construction under the State Council shall, under the guidance of the national medium- and long-term special plan for energy conservation, formulate a national plan for energy conservation in civil buildings, which shall be aligned with relevant plans.
The competent departments of construction under local people's governments at or above the county level shall organize the formulation of plans for energy conservation in civil buildings within their respective administrative regions, and submit them to the people's government at the corresponding level for approval before implementation.

Article 7 The State shall establish and improve the standard system for energy conservation in civil buildings. The national standards for energy conservation in civil buildings shall be developed under the organization of the competent department of construction under the State Council and promulgated in accordance with statutory procedures.
The State encourages the formulation and adoption of local standards for energy conservation in civil buildings that are superior to national standards.

Article 8 People's governments at or above the county level shall allocate funds for energy conservation in civil buildings to support scientific and technological research on and standard-setting for energy conservation in civil buildings, energy-saving renovation of the building envelopes and heating systems of existing buildings, application of renewable energy sources, and promotion of demonstration projects and energy-saving projects for energy conservation in civil buildings.
The government shall guide financial institutions to provide support for projects such as energy-saving renovation of existing buildings, application of renewable energy sources, and demonstration projects for energy conservation in civil buildings.
Energy conservation projects for civil buildings shall enjoy tax preferences according to law.

Article 9 The State shall actively promote the reform of the heating system, improve the heating price formation mechanism, encourage the development of central heating, and gradually implement a system of charging according to the amount of heat used.

Article 10 Entities and individuals that have made remarkable contributions in the work of energy conservation in civil buildings shall be commended and rewarded in accordance with relevant state provisions.

Article 11 The State shall promote the use of new technologies, new processes, new materials and new equipment for energy conservation in civil buildings, and restrict or prohibit the use of technologies, processes, materials and equipment with high energy consumption. The competent department of energy conservation work under the State Council and the competent department of construction shall formulate, publish and timely update the directory of technologies, processes, materials and equipment that are promoted, restricted or prohibited.
The State shall restrict or prohibit the import of technologies, materials and equipment with high energy consumption.
Construction entities, design entities and construction entities shall not use technologies, processes, materials and equipment listed in the directory of prohibited use in construction activities.

Article 12 When preparing detailed urban plans and detailed town plans, the layout, shape and orientation of buildings shall be determined in accordance with the requirements for energy conservation in civil buildings.
The competent department of urban and rural planning shall, when conducting planning review of civil buildings according to law, seek the opinions of the competent department of construction at the same level on whether the design scheme conforms to the mandatory standards for energy conservation in civil buildings; the competent department of construction shall provide its opinions within 10 days from the date of receiving the materials for consultation. The time for consultation shall not be counted in the time limit for planning permission.
Where the design scheme does not conform to the mandatory standards for energy conservation in civil buildings, the construction project planning permit shall not be issued.

Article 13 The review agency for construction drawing design documents shall review the construction drawing design documents in accordance with the mandatory standards for energy conservation in civil buildings; if the reviewed documents do not conform to the mandatory standards for energy conservation in civil buildings, the competent department of construction under the local people's government at or above the county level shall not issue a construction permit.

Article 14 A construction entity shall not expressly or impliedly instruct the design entity or construction entity to design or construct in violation of the mandatory standards for energy conservation in civil buildings, nor shall it expressly or impliedly instruct the construction entity to use wall materials, thermal insulation materials, doors and windows, heating and air conditioning systems, and lighting equipment that do not meet the requirements of the construction drawing design documents.
Where the construction entity procures wall materials, thermal insulation materials, doors and windows, heating and air conditioning systems, and lighting equipment as agreed in the contract, it shall ensure that they meet the requirements of the construction drawing design documents.

Article 15 Design entities, construction entities, project supervision entities and their registered practicing personnel shall design, construct and supervise in accordance with the mandatory standards for energy conservation in civil buildings.

Article 16 A construction entity shall inspect wall materials, thermal insulation materials, doors and windows, heating and air conditioning systems, and lighting equipment entering the construction site; those not meeting the requirements of the construction drawing design documents shall not be used.
If a project supervision entity discovers that the construction entity does not carry out construction in accordance with the mandatory standards for energy conservation in civil buildings, it shall require the construction entity to make corrections; if the construction entity refuses to make corrections, the project supervision entity shall promptly report to the construction entity and to the relevant competent department.
When the insulation works of walls and roofs are being constructed, the supervising engineer shall, in accordance with the requirements of project supervision standards, carry out supervision in the forms of on-site supervision, patrol inspection and parallel inspection.
Without the signature of the supervising engineer, wall materials, thermal insulation materials, doors and windows, heating and air conditioning systems, and lighting equipment shall not be used or installed on the building, and the construction entity shall not proceed with the next process.

Article 17 When organizing the completion acceptance, a construction entity shall inspect whether the civil building conforms to the mandatory standards for energy conservation in civil buildings; if it does not conform to such standards, the construction entity shall not issue a completion acceptance report.

Article 18 Buildings with central heating shall be equipped with heating system control devices, heat metering devices and indoor temperature control devices; public buildings shall also be equipped with sub-metering devices for electricity consumption. The heat metering devices installed in residential buildings shall meet the requirements for household-based metering.
Metering devices shall be verified as qualified according to law.
Article 19 Public corridors, stairways and other parts of buildings shall be installed with and use energy-saving lamps and electrical control devices.

Article 20 For buildings that have conditions for using renewable energy sources, the construction entity shall select appropriate renewable energy sources for heating, cooling, lighting and hot water supply; the design entity shall carry out the design in accordance with the relevant standards for the utilization of renewable energy sources.
The construction of facilities for utilizing renewable energy sources shall be designed, constructed and accepted simultaneously with the main building project.

Article 21 Owners of office buildings of state organs and large public buildings shall conduct assessment and labeling of the buildings' energy efficiency, and publish the assessment results in accordance with relevant state provisions to accept social supervision.
Office buildings of state organs shall be installed with and use energy-saving equipment.
For the purpose of these Regulations, "large public buildings" means public buildings with a single building area of 20,000 square meters or more.

Article 22 When selling commercial housing, a real estate development enterprise shall clearly indicate to the purchaser the energy consumption indicators, energy-saving measures and protection requirements, warranty period of thermal insulation works, and other information of the commercial housing being sold, and shall state such information in the commercial housing sale contract, the residential quality warranty, and the residential use instruction manual.

Article 23 Under normal use conditions, the minimum warranty period for thermal insulation works shall be 5 years. The warranty period for thermal insulation works shall be calculated from the date of completion of acceptance.
If a quality problem occurs within the warranty scope and warranty period of thermal insulation works, the construction entity shall perform the warranty obligations and bear compensation liability for the losses caused according to law.

Article 24 Energy-saving renovation of existing buildings shall be implemented in a planned, step-by-step and categorized manner based on the actual local economic and social development level, geographical and climatic conditions, and other factors.
For the purpose of these Regulations, "energy-saving renovation of existing buildings" means activities to implement energy-saving renovation of the building envelopes, heating systems, heating and air conditioning systems, lighting equipment, hot water supply facilities, etc., of existing buildings that do not conform to the mandatory standards for energy conservation in civil buildings.

Article 25 The competent departments of construction under local people's governments at or above the county level shall organize surveys, statistics and analysis on the construction years, structural forms, energy-consuming systems, energy consumption indicators, life cycles, etc., of existing buildings within their respective administrative regions, formulate plans for energy-saving renovation of existing buildings, specify the objectives, scope and requirements of such renovation, and submit them to the people's government at the corresponding level for approval before organizing implementation.
The energy-saving renovation of existing buildings of central state organs shall be planned and organized by the relevant agency in charge of administrative affairs.

Article 26 For energy-saving renovation of office buildings of state organs and public buildings invested by the government or mainly by the government, a energy-saving renovation plan shall be formulated, fully demonstrated, and relevant approval procedures shall be handled in accordance with relevant state provisions before such renovation may be carried out.
People's governments at all levels and their relevant departments and entities shall not, in violation of relevant state provisions and standards, expand or rebuild existing buildings under the name of energy-saving renovation.

Article 27 For residential buildings and other public buildings other than those prescribed in Article 26 of these Regulations that do not conform to the mandatory standards for energy conservation in civil buildings, energy-saving renovation may be gradually implemented in conjunction with expansion or reconstruction, based on respecting the will of the building owners.

Article 28 The implementation of energy-saving renovation of existing buildings shall conform to the mandatory standards for energy conservation in civil buildings, and low-cost renovation measures such as shading and improving ventilation shall be given priority.
The renovation of the building envelope and the renovation of the heating system of existing buildings shall be carried out simultaneously.

Article 29 When carrying out energy-saving renovation of buildings with central heating, heating system control devices and heat metering devices shall be installed; when carrying out energy-saving renovation of public buildings, indoor temperature control devices and sub-metering devices for electricity consumption shall also be installed.

Article 30 The costs for energy-saving renovation of office buildings of state organs shall be included in the fiscal budget of the people's governments at or above the county level at the corresponding level.
The costs for energy-saving renovation of residential buildings and public buildings used for public welfare purposes such as education, science, culture, health, and sports shall be borne jointly by the government and the building owners.
The State encourages social funds to invest in energy-saving renovation of existing buildings.

Article 31 The owner or user of a building shall ensure the normal operation of the building's energy-consuming systems and shall not intentionally damage the building envelope and energy-consuming systems.
The owners or users of office buildings of state organs and large public buildings shall establish and improve management systems and operating procedures for energy conservation in civil buildings, monitor and maintain the building's energy-consuming systems, and regularly report the sub-metered electricity consumption to the competent department of construction under the local people's government at or above the county level.

Article 32 The competent department of energy conservation work under a local people's government at or above the county level shall, jointly with the competent department of construction at the same level, determine the key electricity-consuming entities for public buildings within its administrative region and their annual electricity consumption limits.
The competent department of construction under a local people's government at or above the county level shall conduct surveys, statistics and evaluation analysis on the electricity consumption of office buildings of state organs and public buildings within its administrative region. The energy consumption for heating, cooling and lighting of office buildings of state organs and large public buildings shall be published to the public in accordance with laws, administrative regulations and other relevant state provisions.
The owners or users of office buildings of state organs and public buildings shall cooperate with the survey and statistics work of the competent department of construction under the local people's government at or above the county level.

Article 33 Heat supply units shall establish and improve relevant systems, and strengthen education and training of professional and technical personnel.
Heat supply units shall improve technical equipment, implement metering management, monitor and maintain the heating system, enhance the efficiency of the heating system, and ensure that the operation of the heating system conforms to the mandatory standards for energy conservation in civil buildings.

Article 34 The competent departments of construction under local people's governments at or above the county level shall conduct surveys, statistics and analysis on the energy consumption of heat supply units within their respective administrative regions, and formulate energy consumption indicators for heat supply units; where the energy consumption exceeds the indicators, they shall require the heat supply units to formulate corresponding improvement measures and supervise their implementation.

Article 36 Where, in violation of these Regulations, people's governments at all levels, their relevant departments or entities, in violation of relevant state provisions and standards, expand or rebuild existing buildings under the name of energy-saving renovation, the persons in charge with responsibility and other directly liable persons shall be given sanctions according to law.

Article 38 Where, in violation of these Regulations, a construction entity issues a completion acceptance report for a civil building project that does not conform to the mandatory standards for energy conservation in civil buildings, the competent department of construction under the local people's government at or above the county level shall order it to make corrections and impose a fine of not less than 2% but not more than 4% of the contract price of the civil building project; if losses are caused, it shall bear compensation liability according to law.

Article 39 Where, in violation of these Regulations, a design entity fails to carry out design in accordance with the mandatory standards for energy conservation in civil buildings, or uses technologies, processes, materials or equipment listed in the directory of prohibited use, the competent department of construction under the local people's government at or above the county level shall order it to make corrections and impose a fine of not less than 100,000 yuan but not more than 300,000 yuan; if the circumstances are serious, the department that issued the qualification certificate shall order it to suspend operations for rectification, lower its qualification grade, or revoke the qualification certificate; if losses are caused, it shall bear compensation liability according to law.

Article 40 Where, in violation of these Regulations, a construction entity fails to carry out construction in accordance with the mandatory standards for energy conservation in civil buildings, the competent department of construction under the local people's government at or above the county level shall order it to make corrections and impose a fine of not less than 2% but not more than 4% of the contract price of the civil building project; if the circumstances are serious, the department that issued the qualification certificate shall order it to suspend operations for rectification, lower its qualification grade, or revoke the qualification certificate; if losses are caused, it shall bear compensation liability according to law.

Article 42 Where, in violation of these Regulations, a project supervision entity commits any of the following acts, the competent department of construction under the local people's government at or above the county level shall order it to make corrections within a time limit; if it fails to make corrections within the time limit, a fine of not less than 100,000 yuan but not more than 300,000 yuan shall be imposed; if the circumstances are serious, the department that issued the qualification certificate shall order it to suspend operations for rectification, lower its qualification grade, or revoke the qualification certificate; if losses are caused, it shall bear compensation liability according to law:
(1) failing to carry out supervision in accordance with the mandatory standards for energy conservation in civil buildings;
(2) failing to carry out supervision in the forms of on-site supervision, patrol inspection and parallel inspection when the insulation works of walls and roofs are being constructed.
Where a supervising engineer signs certifying that wall materials, thermal insulation materials, doors and windows, heating and air conditioning systems, or lighting equipment that do not meet the requirements of the construction drawing design documents meet such requirements, the penalty shall be imposed in accordance with the provisions of Article 67 of the Regulations on the Administration of Quality of Construction Projects.

Article 43 Where, in violation of these Regulations, a real estate development enterprise, when selling commercial housing, fails to clearly indicate to the purchaser the energy consumption indicators, energy-saving measures and protection requirements, warranty period of thermal insulation works, and other information of the commercial housing being sold, or the energy consumption indicators indicated to the purchaser are inconsistent with the actual energy consumption, it shall bear civil liability according to law; the competent department of construction under the local people's government at or above the county level shall order it to make corrections within a time limit; if it fails to make corrections within the time limit, a fine of not more than 2% of the total sales amount of the delivered housing shall be imposed; if the circumstances are serious, the department that issued the qualification certificate shall lower its qualification grade or revoke the qualification certificate.

Article 44 Where, in violation of these Regulations, a registered practicing person fails to implement the mandatory standards for energy conservation in civil buildings, the competent department of construction under the people's government at or above the county level shall order him or her to suspend practice for not less than 3 months but not more than 1 year; if the circumstances are serious, the department that issued the qualification certificate shall revoke the practice qualification certificate and shall not allow re-registration within 5 years.
Article 45 These Regulations shall come into force as of October 1, 2008.
